newsitem.title: USA: High consumer confidence seen in '97 -- Conf Board.
newsitem.headline: High consumer confidence seen in '97 -- Conf Board.

text.p: U.S. consumer confidence is likely to remain high in coming months and may already be adding to consumer spending, said an economist at The Conference Board.
The Conference Board's index of consumer confidence read 118.4 in February, down only slightly from January's revised 118.7 reading.

Jobs growth and growing wages "suggest ... we're going to get these kinds of (confidence) numbers over the next couple of months," said Conference Board senior economist Ken Goldstein in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
Asked whether high confidence will impact consumer spending in the first quarter, Goldstein said, "I think it already is."
Although housing starts dipped in December and January, the housing market should rebound by March in part because of consumers' greater willingness to spend, he said.

Turning to interest rates, Goldstein said the Federal Reserve is taking its policy cues from the Treasury market. "As long as the bond market stays quiet, there's a chance the Fed will continue to stay on the sidelines," he said.
But Goldstein said he expects long-term interest rates to pick up by yearend, a situation he said would make the Fed more likely to raise short-term rates.
"Before the end of the year we're going to see higher interest rates, and conceivably much higher interest rates," he said.
